text: The applicant was born in 1982.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant lives in Baku.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: At the material time the applicant was a member of an opposition party called Musavat.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant attempted to participate in a demonstration organised by the opposition on 20 October 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Prior to the assembly of 20 October 2012, on 15 October 2012, the organisers gave notice to the relevant authority, the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration at the place indicated by the organisers.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) proposed a different location for the demonstration on the outskirts of Baku.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Despite the Baku City Executive Authority's refusal to authorise the demonstration at the originally indicated place, the organisers decided to hold the demonstration as planned.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the applicant, the demonstration of 20 October 2012 was intended to be peaceful.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the applicant, the demonstration of 20 October 2012 was conducted in a peaceful manner.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The participants in the demonstration of 20 October 2012 were demanding democratic reforms in the country.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant had intended to attend the demonstration of 20 October 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant and a few others attempted to march from the headquarters of the Musavat party to the place where the assembly of 20 October 2012 was being held.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Shortly after the applicant's attempt to march to the assembly on 20 October 2012, he was arrested and taken to a police station.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the applicant, he was arrested on 20 October 2012 by people in plain clothes.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 6 May 2014 the applicant participated in an assembly that took place near the Baku Court of Serious Crimes.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The assembly of 6 May 2014 near the Baku Court of Serious Crimes was held in support of members of an opposition group called Nida, who were being tried on that day.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 6 May 2014 the courtroom of the Baku Court of Serious Crimes was full, so some people were waiting outside the court for the outcome of the proceedings.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: When the Baku Court of Serious Crimes announced its judgment on 6 May 2014, those who had gathered outside began to protest against the judgment, which they considered unfair.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The protest outside the Baku Court of Serious Crimes on 6 May 2014 was brief, spontaneous and peaceful.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: As soon as the protesters outside the Baku Court of Serious Crimes on 6 May 2014 started chanting slogans, police officers and people in plain clothes began to forcibly disperse the assembly.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation of the assembly outside the Baku Court of Serious Crimes on 6 May 2014.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: After his arrest on 6 May 2014, the applicant was taken to a police station, where he was kept overnight.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In both cases (20 October 2012 and 6 May 2014), on the day of the applicant's arrest, an administrative-offence report (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) was issued in respect of the applicant.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In the first case (20 October 2012), the administrative-offence report stated that by deliberately failing to comply with a lawful order of the police, the applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In the second case (6 May 2014), the applicant was charged with an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO), which concerns participation in a public assembly that had not been organised in accordance with the law.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the applicant, he was never served with copies of the administrative-offence reports in his case files in either case.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the applicant, he was never served with other documents in his case files in either case.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In both cases (20 October 2012 and 6 May 2014), the applicant was not given access to a lawyer after his arrest or while in police custody.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In the second case (6 May 2014), according to a document drawn up by a police officer and an order dated 6 May 2014, a State-funded lawyer (Mr S.A.) was instructed to assist the applicant.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In the first case, the applicant was brought before the Binagadi District Court on 20 October 2012, the day of his arrest.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: In the second case, the applicant was brought before the Nasimi District Court on 7 May 2014, the day following his arrest.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: According to the applicant, the hearing before the court in both cases (before the Binagadi District Court on 20 October 2012 and before the Nasimi District Court on 7 May 2014) was very brief.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: According to the applicant, members of the public, including human rights defenders and journalists, were not allowed to attend the hearings in either case, even though the court had not taken a formal decision to close the hearing to the public.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: According to the applicant, in neither case was he given an opportunity to hire a lawyer of his own choice for the first-instance court hearings.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: In both cases (before the Binagadi District Court on 20 October 2012 and before the Nasimi District Court on 7 May 2014), State-funded lawyers were appointed to assist the applicant.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: In the second case (before the Nasimi District Court on 7 May 2014), the State-funded lawyer appointed to assist the applicant was Mr S.A., the same lawyer who had been instructed to assist the applicant in accordance with the document of 6 May 2014 drawn up by a police officer.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: According to the records of the court hearings in both cases, in their oral submissions the State-funded lawyers briefly stated that the applicant was not guilty.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: According to the records of the court hearings in both cases, in their oral submissions the State-funded lawyers asked the respective court to discontinue the case.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: In both cases, the only witnesses questioned during the court hearing were police officers who, according to the official records, had arrested the applicant or prepared an administrative-offence report on him.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: The police officer witnesses in both cases testified that the applicant had staged an unauthorised protest.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: In both cases, the first-instance court found that the applicant had failed to stop participating in an unauthorised protest.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: By a decision of 20 October 2012, the Binagadi District Court convicted the applicant under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) and sentenced him to ten days' administrative detention.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: By a decision of 7 May 2014, the Nasimi District Court convicted the applicant under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) and sentenced him to fifteen days' administrative detention.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: On unspecified dates the applicant lodged appeals before the Baku Court of Appeal against his convictions in both cases.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: In his appeals before the Baku Court of Appeal, the applicant argued that his convictions were in violation of his rights because the assemblies in which he had participated or attempted to participate had been peaceful.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: In his appeal before the Baku Court of Appeal in the second case (6 May 2014), the applicant additionally argued that the assembly had been spontaneous.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: In his appeals before the Baku Court of Appeal, the applicant complained that his arrests had been unlawful.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: In his appeals before the Baku Court of Appeal, the applicant complained that the hearings before the respective first-instance courts had not been fair.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: In both cases, the applicant was assisted before the Baku Court of Appeal by a lawyer of his own choice.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: On 29 October 2012, the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal in the first case and upheld the decision of the Binagadi District Court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: On 16 May 2014, the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal in the second case and upheld the decision of the Nasimi District Court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
B. Court proceedings against the applicant

text: At the time of both of the applicant's arrests (20 October 2012 and 6 May 2014), under Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS

text: At the time of the applicant's arrest on 20 October 2012, Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 (CAO) provided that any breach of the rules, set forth under the legislation, on the organisation and holding of assemblies, demonstrations, protests, marches and pickets shall be punishable by a reprimand or a fine of seven to thirteen manats (AZN).
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS

text: At the time of the applicant's arrest on 20 October 2012, Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 (CAO) provided that deliberate failure by an individual to comply with a lawful order of a police officer or military serviceman carrying out their duties to protect public order shall be punishable by a fine of twenty to twenty-five manats (AZN) or, if that sanction is inadequate in the circumstances of the case and taking into account the character of the offender, by administrative detention for a term of up to fifteen days.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS

text: Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 entered into force on 1 January 2013.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS

text: Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced new wording to Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) concerning breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS

text: Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies became explicitly punishable under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS

text: Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced for the first time a punishment in the form of administrative detention of up to fifteen days under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS

text: Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced community service as a new form of punishment under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS

text: Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 increased the fine for breaching the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies, fixing the amounts as follows: between AZN 300 and 600 for participants of an assembly; between AZN 1,500 and 3,000 for individuals who organise an assembly; between AZN 3,000 and 6,000 for persons in charge (vəzifəli şəxslər) who organise an assembly; and between AZN 15,000 and 30,000 for legal entities involved in the organisation of an assembly.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS

section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS

text: Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed concern about the restrictive climate for the activities of the extra-parliamentary opposition in Azerbaijan, which complains about limitations imposed on freedom of expression and freedom of assembly and the lack of access to the public media.

section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS

text: Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed deep concern about the situation regarding basic freedoms in Azerbaijan.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS

section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS

section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS

text: In the Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe expressed deep concern about recent amendments to the Law on Freedom of Assembly, the Criminal Code and the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan, which further erode the right to freedom of assembly.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS

text: In the Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe stated that the sanctions which can now be imposed in Azerbaijan, coupled with the fact that local authorities have not authorised a single rally in Baku city centre in recent years, clearly have a chilling effect on the organisation of or participation in demonstrations.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS

text: In the Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe expressed the view that participants in peaceful assemblies should not be sanctioned for the mere fact of being present at and actively participating in the demonstration in question, provided they do not do anything illegal, violent or obscene in the course of it.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS

text: In the Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe urged the Azerbaijani authorities to ensure that no disproportionate sanction, which would undermine the fundamental right to peaceful assembly, is imposed.
